review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp-tagged lemmas (`coe_lt_degree`, `degree_map_eq_iff`, `natDegree_map_eq_iff`, the `nextCoeff_*` lemmas, `degree_add_degree_leadingCoeff_inv`). None looked like a loop or a competing rule. I also checked the neighbouring simp lemmas `degree_mul`, `natDegree_pow`, `degree_pow` and `leadingCoeff_mul` in the Polynomial directory. The one finding is that `natDegree_comp` has no `@[simp]` attribute. It is a judgement call, because I did not test the downstream effect of adding it. The comments that say "`simp` normal form of ..." sit on `degree_leadingCoeff_inv` (not simp) and `degree_add_degree_leadingCoeff_inv` (simp). That is slightly confusing. findings.excerpt: theorem natDegree_comp : natDegree (p.comp q) = natDegree p * natDegree q := by
findings.problem: Over a ring with `NoZeroDivisors`, `natDegree_comp` is an unconditional equation whose right side is built from smaller terms. It is not `@[simp]`, although the sibling lemmas `natDegree_pow` and `degree_mul` are simp and so is the specialisation `natDegree_iterate_comp`, whose proof uses `natDegree_comp`. So `simp` normalises `natDegree (p ^ n)` and `natDegree (p.comp^[k] q)` but leaves `natDegree (p.comp q)` stuck. Several callers have to pass it by hand: `simp [natDegree_comp]` in `Mathlib/Analysis/Polynomial/Order.lean` (lines 92, 101, 108) and `Mathlib/Analysis/Polynomial/Basic.lean` line 124.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `natDegree_comp` with `@[simp]`, exactly as `natDegree_iterate_comp` and `natDegree_pow` are tagged. The rewrite terminates, because it replaces a `comp` by a product of two smaller `natDegree` terms. Afterwards, drop the explicit `natDegree_comp` from the `simp [...]` calls in the files above, wherever they still close the goal without it.
findings.benefit: Goals mentioning `natDegree (p.comp q)` simplify with plain `simp`, as `natDegree (p ^ n)` and the iterate version already do. Callers no longer need to pass the lemma by hand. The simp set also becomes more uniform, since `natDegree_iterate_comp` is simp but its one-step case is not.
